messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] P99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate-stream (us-west1). p99=6.3s, p95=1.8s, SLO p99<=2s. Severity: P1 — paging oncall: ria. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/incidents/streaming-latency — check streaming stalls, GPU node ECC & thermal telemetry, and router fallbacks.

ria: acked — I'll take first touch. grabbing traces and impact. @samir can you pull p95/p99 by model and by route? also posting current alert graph. :eyes:

samir: grabbing metrics now. short summary: overall qps steady ~420r/s, but streaming tail has huge variance. by-model p99: gpt-large-v1=6.1s, gpt-medium-v1=3.9s. Top route is /v1/generate-stream. Not seeing application errors, just long stalls during token stream flush.

ria: ok. any node-level signals? kevin, can infra share GPU telemetry?

kevin: looking. a subset of nodes in us-west1-gpu-pool-2 show rising correctable ECC counts and temp jumps. sample: node gpu-uw2-17: ECC_correctable last_10m=430 -> 1210, temp_avg 83C -> 90C. also dmesg shows repeated NVML warnings.

elaine: joining. that ECC spike correlates with streaming stalls we've seen in other incidents. probable kernel-level retries causing stalls in the fast-path. can we isolate affected pods and route traffic off those nodes? Suggest cordon+drain then route fallback to cpu instances for streaming sessions >30s.

ria: doing quick sweep. running: 
```
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running -n inference | grep uw2-17
kubectl cordon gpu-uw2-17
kubectl drain gpu-uw2-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force -n inference
```

samir: adding router change: update smart-router policy to downrank uw2 pool by preference and enable model-variant fallback to quantized variant (gpt-large-q4) for new sessions. patch applied: route weight uw2=0.2 -> 0.05.

maria: from support — any estimate on customer impact? we have a paying customer seeing repeated stream hangups. need list of affected API keys and escalation list.

samir: quick count: ~24 API keys with 5+ stalled streams in last 15m; top two tenants: acme-ml and shoplane. I'll export logs and provide session ids. example trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.

kevin: we attempted soft-reset on gpu-uw2-17's driver and NVML, but ECC continued to climb. sounds like hardware aging + thermal saturation. planning hot-swap for 2 nodes, but that's ~30-45m. in interim we should throttle long-lived streaming and prefer cached KV responses.

elaine: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) route away from affected GPU nodes (in progress), 2) enable intelligent early-response: if token delay > 2s, send keepalive chunk and consider ephemeral fallback to CPU generation for current session, 3) schedule rolling reboot/hotswap for flagged machines.

ria: executing step 1 now. cordoned 3 nodes: gpu-uw2-17, gpu-uw2-21, gpu-uw2-05. drain succeeded for 21, 05 drained with one Pod failing - forced deleted. active sessions for those pods will reconnect and hit fallback.

oncall-desk: auto-note: incident status -> mitigation in progress. ETA for full pool recovery estimated 2 hrs. please update when you have customer list for notifications.

samir: sending list to @maria via DM + SRE-runbook export. attaching quick grep output (snip):
```
2026-03-15T14:10:12Z trace-0a1b2c3d token-stream: stall after 34s, gpu node gpu-uw2-17 nvml_warn: ECC CORRECTABLE 1123
2026-03-15T14:12:05Z trace-1f2e3d4c token-stream: stall after 12s, fallback->cpu
```

maria: thanks. I'll open priority support tickets for acme-ml & shoplane and prepare customer-facing note: short explanation + mitigation + ETA.

kevin: hardware team thinks ECC is ramping because a thermal fan on uw2-17 is intermittently dropping RPM under load — likely firmware bug + dust. hot-swap confirmed for uw2-17 and uw2-05, parts on-site.

elaine: while we wait for swap, can we enable server-side token rate-limiter for streaming sessions to reduce sustained GPU load? small throttle to 18 tokens/sec for new streams; existing ones get fallback.

ria: rate-limiter toggle applied to us-west cluster. monitoring p99 now. initial p99 dropped to 3.4s (from 6.3s) after routing change + throttling. still above SLO but trending down.

samir: note — streaming stalls cause client reconnect storms; recommend soft-505s for long stalls to limit retries. adding that to router config.

maria: customer comms drafted: "We're investigating an increase in streaming latency for customers in US-West. We've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; some sessions may be short-lived, we're working on hardware replacements and will provide updates." sending now.

kevin: hardware swap started for uw2-17. techs report node offline for parts replacement. expected node back in ~40m.

ria: handing ongoing operations to elaine for post-incident cleanup and RCA. I'll remain available for customer follow-ups. elaine — please own the timeline and write-up. samir — prepare timeline of metrics and traces for RCA. kevin — pls include hardware telemetry and replacement notes. maria — any follow-ups from customers?

elaine: taking post-incident. will collect artifacts and create incident ticket INC-2026-03-15-01 with timeline, root cause hypothesis (thermal + ECC causing kernel retries -> streaming stalls), and remediation actions (fan firmware, dust checks, expanded telemetry on ECC rates).

ria: thanks team. final update before handoff: current p99=1.9s (after two nodes swapped and rate limit), p95=1.2s. marking incident as mitigated — continuing monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity downgraded to P3 pending RCA. postmortem owner: elaine.

oncall-desk: handoff complete — elaine is now incident owner. please add any remaining notes to INC-2026-03-15-01. :white_check_mark:
